APP.name: Authorized Push Payment & Social Engineering
APP.thesis: The victim authenticates correctly and pushes the money themselves. Every credential-centric control passes, so detection must reason about intent and counterparty rather than identity.

ATO.name: Account Takeover & Authentication Subversion
ATO.thesis: GenAI synthesises the physical and behavioural traits that replaced passwords, collapsing voice, face and behaviour into forgeable artefacts.

ID.name: Identity Fabrication & Onboarding Abuse
ID.thesis: Generative models solved the supply-chain problem for identity: faces, documents and liveness are now manufactured on demand at near-zero marginal cost.

CARD.name: Card, Merchant & Dispute Abuse
CARD.thesis: Automation industrialises the long tail of card fraud and weaponises the consumer protection machinery itself.

AGENTIC.name: Agentic Commerce & Delegated Authority
AGENTIC.thesis: When an AI agent holds delegated payment authority, the attack surface moves from the human's psychology to the agent's context window. Every transaction is technically authorised; only the intent is hijacked.

RAIL.name: Payment Rail & Messaging Infrastructure
RAIL.thesis: Instant, irrevocable rails compress the intervention window to milliseconds while richer message schemas widen the semantic attack surface.

MULE.name: Mule Networks, Layering & Cash-out
MULE.thesis: The receiving side of the transaction. Under mandatory reimbursement regimes this is now a direct balance-sheet liability, not someone else's problem.

MODEL.name: Attacks on the Defence Itself
MODEL.thesis: The fraud model is an asset with an attack surface: it can be probed, evaded, poisoned and reverse-engineered through its own decision feedback.

CRYPTO.name: Digital Asset Rails & DeFi
CRYPTO.thesis: Programmable money compresses vulnerability discovery and exploitation into a single block.

vectors.name: Family emergency voice-clone extortion
vectors.description: Three to fifteen seconds of audio scraped from social media is enough to clone a relative's voice. The victim receives a distressed call from a "child" or "parent" demanding an immediate instant transfer for bail, medical fees or an accident.
vectors.liability_note: Reimbursable under UK PSR mandatory regime; 50/50 sending/receiving PSP split.

vectors.name: Executive voice-clone wire instruction
vectors.description: A cloned CFO or CEO voice calls a treasury or accounts-payable operator with an urgent, confidential payment instruction, often referencing a real in-flight deal harvested from press releases and filings.

vectors.name: Multi-party deepfake video conference authorisation
vectors.description: Attackers populate an entire video call with deepfaked colleagues so the victim sees familiar faces approving a transfer. Demonstrated at scale by the USD 25.6M Arup loss, where every participant except the victim was synthetic.

vectors.name: LLM-authored vendor invoice redirection
vectors.description: A dark LLM ingests a compromised mailbox thread and emits a bank-detail change request in the exact lexicon, formatting and sign-off of the real supplier. The invoice PDF is regenerated with the mule account substituted.
vectors.liability_note: USD 2.77B across 21,442 BEC incidents in FBI IC3 2024 reporting.

vectors.name: Bank/police impersonation with remote-access "safe account" transfer
vectors.description: A synthetic voice posing as the bank's fraud team convinces the victim their account is compromised and walks them through installing a screen-sharing or remote-access tool, then dictates a transfer to a "safe account" the attacker controls.

vectors.name: LLM-run relationship investment grooming
vectors.description: Malicious LLMs sustain thousands of concurrent, culturally fluent conversations over weeks, then escalate the victim through a fake trading platform. Escalating payments to a small set of accounts, with a final large "withdrawal fee" liquidation.

vectors.name: Deepfake celebrity endorsement investment scam
vectors.description: Photoreal deepfakes of recognisable figures promote a fraudulent trading platform or token pool on short-form video, driving retail victims to fund a mule or smart contract directly.

vectors.name: AI-generated marketplace listing purchase scam
vectors.description: Entire storefronts, product photography and review corpora are generated in minutes. The victim pays by push payment for goods that never ship, and the storefront is rotated before disputes accumulate.

vectors.name: UPI collect / pull-request approval manipulation
vectors.description: India-specific: the attacker sends a *collect* (pull) request framed as an incoming refund or cashback. The victim approves with their UPI PIN believing they are receiving money, and debits their own account instead.

vectors.name: Gen Alpha in-game grooming to in-app purchase extraction
vectors.description: Attackers use platform-native slang and engineered dopamine loops on gaming and short-video platforms to groom minors into executing purchases or gift-card transfers on a parent's stored credential. The device, IP and geolocation are all legitimate household values, so conventional device risk fails.

vectors.name: Synthetic-voice refund / overpayment reversal scam
vectors.description: A cloned support voice claims an accidental overpayment and requests the victim "return the difference" by instant transfer, often after showing a doctored confirmation screen via screen share.

vectors.name: Tax authority / regulator impersonation
vectors.description: Deepfaked officials and perfectly localised notices demand immediate settlement of a fabricated tax demand or customs duty, exploiting institutional authority and statutory deadlines.

vectors.name: Synthetic disaster-relief charity appeal
vectors.description: Generative imagery and video of an unfolding disaster drive high-velocity, low-value donations to freshly registered collection accounts, exploiting the compressed decision window of genuine emergencies.

vectors.name: AI-run task / gig prepayment scam
vectors.description: Automated recruiters onboard victims into a fake gig platform that pays small task rewards before requiring escalating "deposit to unlock" payments. The conversational layer is fully LLM-operated across thousands of concurrent victims.

vectors.name: Attacker-operated deepfake contact centre (callback lure)
vectors.description: Rather than calling the victim, the attacker plants a fake support number in search results or an invoice, then runs a fully synthetic IVR and agent stack so the victim initiates contact — defeating "we will never call you" consumer education.

vectors.name: Voice-biometric bypass in IVR and contact centre
vectors.description: Commodity synthetic speech first navigates the IVR to enumerate balances and account state, then a high-fidelity clone engages a human agent to force a credential reset or wire authorisation. Cloning has crossed the threshold where legacy voiceprint engines and human listeners cannot discriminate.

vectors.name: SIM swap with LLM-assisted carrier social engineering
vectors.description: An LLM scripts the carrier retention conversation to port the victim's number, after which every SMS OTP flows to the attacker. Payments then originate from a new device with perfectly valid one-time codes.

vectors.name: Synthetic behavioural-biometric trajectories
vectors.description: Models trained on human interaction telemetry emit keystroke flight times, pointer jitter and acceleration curves inside the acceptance band of continuous authentication engines, defeating the standard-deviation thresholds those engines use.

vectors.name: Adversary-in-the-middle phishing kit with session-token capture
vectors.description: A reverse-proxy phishing kit, scaffolded and localised by an LLM, relays the real login and captures the post-MFA session cookie. The subsequent payment carries a fully authenticated session from attacker infrastructure.

vectors.name: On-device overlay / accessibility-service payment hijack
vectors.description: Malware delivered through an LLM-generated lure abuses accessibility services to read the screen, overlay a fake confirmation and mutate the payee at the moment of authorisation. The transaction originates from the genuine device and credential.

vectors.name: Knowledge-based authentication defeat via OSINT agents
vectors.description: Autonomous scraping agents assemble a dossier from social profiles, breach corpora and public records, letting the attacker answer every knowledge-based challenge correctly on the first attempt.

vectors.name: Forced authenticator downgrade to weaker factor
vectors.description: The attacker triggers a synthetic failure of the strong authenticator (device loss, biometric failure) to push the session onto a legacy fallback such as SMS OTP or a voice print, both of which are now forgeable.

vectors.name: Synthetic identity cultivation and credit bust-out
vectors.description: A GAN-generated face plus a stolen or fabricated national identifier opens an account, then behaves impeccably for months — small, punctual, unremarkable payments — to cultivate a thin credit file, before drawing every available line in a single burst and vanishing.

vectors.name: On-demand synthetic KYC document generation
vectors.description: Fraud-as-a-service platforms mint driving licences, utility bills, pay stubs and bank statements against arbitrary templates in seconds, defeating document-OCR and template-matching checks at onboarding.

vectors.name: Virtual camera injection against remote liveness
vectors.description: Rather than presenting a deepfake to a physical sensor — which leaves moire and optical artefacts — the attacker installs a virtual camera driver and injects a rendered or real-time face-swapped stream directly into the application layer, bypassing the sensor entirely.

vectors.name: Physiologically coherent deepfake defeating rPPG liveness
vectors.description: Remote photoplethysmography assumed deepfakes could not reproduce the blood-volume pulse visible in skin chrominance. Diffusion-based generators now inadvertently carry the driving actor's pulse into the output, and aggressive video compression strips the residual artefacts detectors relied on — collapsing both the signal and the defence.

vectors.name: Automated account-opening farm for mule supply
vectors.description: Agentic browser automation plus synthetic identity kits (available for a few dollars each) opens hundreds of accounts per day across PSPs, creating the receiving-side inventory that every push-payment scam depends on.

vectors.name: Biometric template inversion from breached vaults
vectors.description: Generative models reconstruct a usable face or voice from leaked biometric template vectors, converting a one-time data breach into permanent, unrevocable authentication compromise.

vectors.name: Authorised-user tradeline farming for synthetic credit files
vectors.description: Synthetic personas are attached as authorised users to seasoned real tradelines, inheriting credit history instantly and compressing the cultivation phase of a bust-out from months to weeks.

vectors.name: Automated card testing and non-VBV BIN enumeration
vectors.description: Dark-LLM tooling identifies BIN ranges that lack secondary authentication, then distributed bots validate stolen PANs with micro-authorisations against low-friction merchants before the good cards are resold or cashed out.

vectors.name: Low-and-slow distributed authorisation probing
vectors.description: A patient variant of card testing that spreads probes across thousands of IPs, merchants and hours specifically to stay under per-merchant and per-BIN velocity thresholds, defeating rate-based rules by construction.

vectors.name: Synthetic-voice refund and chargeback abuse at scale
vectors.description: Cloned customer voices call merchant support to report non-delivery or defects, industrialising return and chargeback abuse. Refund and dispute abuse is already a ~USD 103B global problem; voice automation removes its labour ceiling.

vectors.name: Front-merchant transaction laundering with generated legitimacy
vectors.description: A benign-looking storefront — complete with AI-generated inventory, policies and review history — is onboarded to process card volume for a prohibited or fraudulent business, misrepresenting the true MCC to the acquirer.

vectors.name: Exploitation of risk-based frictionless 3DS flows
vectors.description: Attackers shape transaction attributes — amount bands, merchant category, device consistency — to land inside the issuer's frictionless-approval envelope, avoiding any challenge while carrying stolen credentials.

vectors.name: Fraudulent wallet token provisioning ("yellow path" defeat)
vectors.description: A stolen PAN is provisioned into an attacker-controlled wallet by defeating the issuer's identification-and-verification step, typically with a cloned voice at the call centre. Subsequent payments carry a fully tokenised, device-bound credential.

vectors.name: Generated micro-subscription farms
vectors.description: Networks of synthetic merchants harvest low-value recurring mandates that stay below dispute-worthy thresholds, monetising consumer inattention rather than credential theft.

vectors.name: Indirect prompt injection hijacking agent payment routing
vectors.description: LLMs concatenate system instructions, user intent and retrieved content into one undifferentiated token stream, with no cryptographic boundary between command and data. Adversarial text hidden in a product listing, catalogue or invoice PDF overrides the user's instruction and redirects the payment token. Every API call is technically authorised; only the intent was hijacked.

vectors.name: MCP tool-description poisoning
vectors.description: Malicious instructions are embedded in the metadata or description of a tool the agent is permitted to call. With auto-approve enabled the agent executes them silently, exfiltrating credentials or invoking payment tools out of policy.

vectors.name: Over-scoped MCP server acting as a confused deputy
vectors.description: The agent's server holds broader authority than the delegating user, so an attacker who can influence the agent's context borrows that excess authority to reach resources and payment scopes the user never granted.

vectors.name: Agent-optimised counterfeit storefront (AEO poisoning)
vectors.description: Where earlier scam sites were built to fool human eyes, these are built to fool machine buyers: fabricated structured product data, synthetic review corpora and artificially low landed cost, tuned so an autonomous shopping agent optimising for price selects them without any human ever looking at the page.

vectors.name: Shared Payment Token theft, replay and scope stretching
vectors.description: Scoped, time-bound agent credentials are stolen through device compromise or a dependency supply chain and replayed. Because the token, merchant relationship and shipping address are all already trusted, the fraudulent transaction sits precisely on the victim's behavioural baseline.

vectors.name: Impersonation of trusted commerce agents
vectors.description: Merchants grant recognised AI shopping agents reduced friction and privileged catalogue access. Fraudsters spoof those user-agent strings and behavioural fingerprints to inherit that trust — millions of spoofed requests against major agent identities have been recorded in single two-month windows.

vectors.name: Silent cart stuffing and high-margin add-on injection
vectors.description: An injected instruction adds digital gift cards or high-margin items to the agent's cart just before checkout. The primary purchase is exactly what the user asked for, so the anomaly hides inside a legitimate order.

vectors.name: Persistent agent memory poisoning
vectors.description: Rather than a one-shot injection, the payload is written into the agent's long-term memory or user-preference store, so the malicious routing rule survives session boundaries and reactivates on future, unrelated purchases.

vectors.name: Adversarial merchant agent exploiting buyer-agent utility
vectors.description: In agent-to-agent negotiation the seller's agent probes the buyer agent's objective function — bundling, urgency framing, decoy pricing — to extract a worse deal or steer to a higher-fee rail, a machine-speed analogue of dark patterns.

vectors.name: Agent-established recurring mandate rug pull
vectors.description: The agent is steered into accepting a recurring mandate or auto-renewal during an otherwise ordinary one-off purchase, converting a single authorisation into a standing claim on the account.

vectors.name: Instant-rail fan-out inside the intervention window
vectors.description: Instant rails settle irrevocably in seconds, compressing the decision window to roughly 300 milliseconds. Attackers split a drained balance into many transfers fired within that window so that even a correct alert lands after settlement.

vectors.name: ISO 20022 semantic field poisoning and model drift induction
vectors.description: The migration to structured ISO 20022 XML gives AML models far richer features — and gives attackers a large, machine-writable semantic surface. Syntactically perfect payloads carry deceptive remittance, intermediary and beneficiary content designed to skew feature weightings and, over time, teach the model that a specific routing pattern is benign.

vectors.name: Confirmation-of-Payee evasion via homoglyph and transliteration
vectors.description: Name-matching checks are defeated with Unicode homoglyphs, transliteration variants and plausible abbreviations that score above the fuzzy-match threshold while naming a different legal entity.

vectors.name: Static merchant QR substitution
vectors.description: A printed merchant QR is overlaid with the attacker's VPA. Payments look like ordinary in-person merchant payments from the payer's side while the funds land in a mule account — high volume, low value, and geographically clustered.

vectors.name: Corridor arbitrage and round-tripping across instant rails
vectors.description: Funds are routed through jurisdictions and interlinked instant-payment corridors chosen for weak information sharing, breaking the transaction graph between the victim's PSP and the ultimate cash-out point.

vectors.name: E-mandate / autopay abuse
vectors.description: Recurring debit authority is obtained under a misleading pretext and then drawn at the maximum permitted amount and frequency, exploiting the fact that mandate execution bypasses per-transaction authentication.

vectors.name: Batch cutoff and settlement-window exploitation
vectors.description: Payments are timed to land immediately after a deferred-settlement cutoff or during holiday windows when review staffing is thinnest, maximising the elapsed time before a human can intervene.

vectors.name: Multi-hop mule fan-out and structuring
vectors.description: Proceeds land in a first-hop mule and are immediately split across many second- and third-hop accounts in amounts below reporting thresholds. Under the UK PSR regime the receiving PSP carries 50% of the reimbursement, making inbound detection a direct balance-sheet problem rather than a courtesy.
vectors.liability_note: UK PSR mandatory reimbursement (from 7 October 2024) splits liability 50/50 between sending and receiving PSP, capped at GBP 85,000 per claim.

vectors.name: Graph-aware structuring designed to defeat GNN detection
vectors.description: Ring topology, hop timing and amount variance are optimised against a surrogate graph model so the laundering subgraph resembles ordinary community structure — no star patterns, no synchronised bursts, no threshold-hugging amounts.

vectors.name: Automated mule recruitment and account renting
vectors.description: LLM-run recruitment campaigns targeting students and gig workers convert legitimate, well-aged accounts into mules, defeating account-age and KYC-quality heuristics.

vectors.name: Peer-to-peer crypto off-ramp liquidation
vectors.description: Laundered fiat is converted through P2P crypto desks and privacy tooling within minutes of settlement, terminating the traceable payment graph.

vectors.name: Gift card and closed-loop value liquidation
vectors.description: Funds are converted into closed-loop stored value that settles instantly and resells at a discount, a favourite terminal hop for scams targeting minors and elderly victims.

vectors.name: Adversarial perturbation of tabular transaction features
vectors.description: The same gradient logic used against image classifiers applies to tabular fraud models: the attacker nudges controllable features along the direction that most reduces the score, subject to the constraint that the payment still achieves its objective. Amount, timing, merchant category and session pacing are all attacker- controlled.

vectors.name: Decision-boundary extraction via approve/decline oracle
vectors.description: Every declined authorisation is a free label. Systematic probing with small, controlled variations reconstructs a surrogate of the issuer's model, which is then used offline to design transactions that score below the alert threshold.

vectors.name: Dispute-channel label poisoning
vectors.description: Supervised fraud models learn from dispute outcomes. Coordinated false disputes — and suppressed true ones — corrupt the label stream itself, degrading the model from inside its own retraining loop.

vectors.name: Slow-boil drift poisoning of transaction monitoring
vectors.description: Low-value, benign-looking transactions are injected over months specifically to shift the model's baseline, so that by the time the real attack runs, its signature already sits inside the learned normal.

vectors.name: Reason-code leakage of the decision boundary
vectors.description: Customer-facing decline reasons and regulator-mandated explanations disclose which features drove a decision, handing the attacker a partial gradient without any need to train a surrogate.

vectors.name: LLM-accelerated smart contract vulnerability discovery
vectors.description: Dark LLMs audit open-source contract code for reentrancy, access-control and oracle flaws far faster than defenders can patch, compressing the window between deployment and exploitation.

vectors.name: Automated flash-loan liquidity drain
vectors.description: Uncollateralised borrow, exploit and repay execute inside a single block. With exploit code now machine-generated, the whole cycle from vulnerability discovery to drained pool collapses to minutes.

vectors.name: Address poisoning of payment history
vectors.description: Dust transactions from vanity addresses that mimic the prefix and suffix of a counterparty's real address contaminate transaction history, so a copy-paste from history sends funds to the attacker.

vectors.name: Deepfake-endorsed token launch and rug pull
vectors.description: A synthetic endorsement from a recognisable figure drives liquidity into a token whose contract permits the deployer to withdraw the entire pool.
